title: Effective generic action and equivariant orbit norms
statement:
Let $S$ be an integral scheme with function field $K$, and let $p:Y\to S$ be a dominant separated morphism with $Y$ integral. Let $J$ be a finite group acting on $Y$ over $S$, let $G$ be its image in $\operatorname{Aut}_S(Y)$, and put $C=Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$. Then restriction $G\to\operatorname{Aut}_K(C)$ is injective. For any invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $L$ put $B=\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*L$ and $\mathcal N_G(a)=\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*a\in\Gamma(Y,B^{\otimes n})$ for $a\in\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes n})$, with the ordered tensor and power comparisons of [def-sfb-pencil-orbit-bundle-norm]. The canonical factor-permutation isomorphisms $h^*B\simeq B$ form a $G$-linearization and carry $h^*\mathcal N_G(a)$ to $\mathcal N_G(a)$. Whenever $\mathcal N_G(a),\mathcal N_G(b)$ generate $B^{\otimes n}$, their section morphism $[\mathcal N_G(a):\mathcal N_G(b)]:Y\to\mathbf P^1_S$ is $J$-invariant. The construction and these identifications commute with restriction to an open of $S$ and with arbitrary base change $T\to S$, using the induced $G$-action even if that action ceases to be faithful. For every $m\geq1$ one has $\mathcal N_G(a^m)=\mathcal N_G(a)^m$ under the canonical tensor-power identification.

Integral schemes, function fields, separated morphisms, and base change have the meanings of [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-sc-function-field], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-pc-base-change]. Invertible modules, generating sections and their projective-coordinate morphisms are [def-sc-invertible-module], [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections]. Dominant means that the image is dense; a $G$-linearization means pullback isomorphisms compatible with multiplication and the identity in $G$.

source.place: de Jong §3.4, printed p.606; agent-written quotient-free norm-section replacement, extracted from returned proof steps 2--3. The last extraction supplies the finite-separable parameter descent needed in §3.3. Local PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read at https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.1575.pdf.

proof.text: Let $\xi$ be the generic point of $Y$ and $\eta$ that of $S$. Continuity gives $p(Y)\subseteq\overline{\{p(\xi)\}}$, so dominance gives $p(\xi)=\eta$. The map on local rings therefore gives $K=\mathcal O_{S,\eta}\to\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}=k(Y)$. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-base-change] supplies $u:\operatorname{Spec}k(Y)\to C$ whose composite with $q:C\to Y$ is the generic-point map $i$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], on every nonempty affine open $V\subset Y$ the map $\mathcal O_Y(V)\to k(Y)$ is injective. These opens are a basis, so $\mathcal O_Y\to i_*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}k(Y)}$ is injective: $i$ is scheme-theoretically dominant.

source.place: Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions; generic-point map and fibre-product factorization

proof.text: Suppose $g_1,g_2\in G$ induce the same automorphism of $C$. Then $g_1\circ i=g_1\circ q\circ u=g_2\circ q\circ u=g_2\circ i$. Apply [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated] with its $T=Y$, target $Y$, base $S$, and $\iota=i$. Its separatedness hypothesis is exactly the separatedness of $p$; its two structure composites are $p$ because $g_1,g_2$ are $S$-automorphisms. Step 1 supplies scheme-theoretic dominance. Thus $g_1=g_2$, proving injectivity. Restriction respects multiplication by the fibre-product universal property, so this is the asserted injective group homomorphism.

source.place: Statement and equalizer proof, applied to the generic-point probe

proof.text: Use the enumeration, unit tail, and recursive comparisons of [def-sfb-pencil-orbit-bundle-norm]. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1), every $g^*L$, hence $B$ and every $B^{\otimes n}$, is invertible (the zero power is $\mathcal O_Y$). By its clause (2), pullback distributes over the ordered tensor and $h^*g^*L\simeq(g\circ h)^*L$. Adopt $(gh)(y)=g(h(y))$. Define $\lambda_h:h^*B\simeq B$ by this comparison followed by the factor permutation sending the factor labelled $g$ to the factor labelled $gh$. This permutation is bijective, with inverse multiplication by $h^{-1}$. The symmetry, associators and unitors of [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-symmetric-monoidal] provide the required ordered permutation map, including its unit tail.

Check the linearization on local pure tensors, which generate the tensor sheaf. In $k^*h^*B$, the factor originally labelled $g$ is $(ghk)^*L$. First applying $k^*\lambda_h$ moves it to label $gh$ in $k^*B$, then $\lambda_k$ moves it to $ghk$ in $B$. Applying $\lambda_{hk}$ directly makes exactly the same move and leaves the same tensor entries. The pullback-composition maps and tensor symmetries in [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2) have these pure-tensor formulas; consequently the two sheaf maps agree. The identity permutation gives $\lambda_1=\mathrm{id}$ under $1^*B\simeq B$. Thus $\lambda_{hk}=\lambda_k\circ k^*\lambda_h$ under $(hk)^*\simeq k^*h^*$, the required cocycle.

source.place: Tags 01CD and 01CA: explicit pullback and permutation formulas; cocycle checked on pure tensors

proof.text: The recursive power-distribution map of [def-sfb-pencil-orbit-bundle-norm] sends the array of factors $(g,r)$, $g\in G$, $1\leq r\leq n$, from the order with $g$ outermost to the order with $r$ outermost. Its pullback-power comparisons send $h^*(s_1\otimes\cdots\otimes s_n)$ to $h^*s_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h^*s_n$, by [def-sc-tensor-pullback-power-comparison] and [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2). Reindexing $(g,r)$ as $(gh,r)$ therefore commutes with this distribution. Hence the tensor-power linearization sends $h^*\mathcal N_G(a)$ to the tensor of $(gh)^*a$ over $g$, which is exactly $\mathcal N_G(a)$ after the permutation of Step 3. For $n=0$, $a$ is a global function and $\mathcal N_G(a)=\prod_{g\in G}g^*a$ under the specified unit maps. Applying $h^*$ permutes these factors by $g\mapsto gh$, so the product is fixed; no assumption $a=1$ is made.

source.place: Tags 01CD and 01CA: pullback of tensors and transposition of a finite array of factors

proof.text: Put $s=\mathcal N_G(a)$ and $t=\mathcal N_G(b)$. They generate the invertible module $B^{\otimes n}$ by hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre], at every point at least one has nonzero image in its fibre; this is the hypothesis of the projective-space theorem below. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points], precomposition of the section morphism with $h$ corresponds to $(h^*B^{\otimes n},h^*s,h^*t)$. Step 5 identifies this pair with $(B^{\otimes n},s,t)$; equivalent pairs give equal maps to $\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$. Since $p\circ h=p$, both maps also have the same component in $S$. The fibre-product uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] now gives $[s:t]\circ h=[s:t]$ over $S$. Every element of $J$ acts through its image in $G$, so the morphism is $J$-invariant.

source.place: Tag 01NE, lemma-projective-space, and paragraph after Definition 01NF

proof.text: For $T\to S$ put $Y_T=Y\times_ST$ and $v:Y_T\to Y$. Each $g$ induces $g_T$ with $v\circ g_T=g\circ v$ [def-pc-base-change]. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] gives $v^*g^*L\simeq g_T^*v^*L$. Tensor these maps in the SAME enumeration of $G$ to identify $v^*B$ with $B_{G,T}$. On local tensors these maps send each entry to its pullback; the unit entry stays $1$. Thus they carry $v^*\mathcal N_G(a)$ to $\mathcal N_{G,T}(v^*a)$ using the recursive power comparisons of [def-sfb-pencil-orbit-bundle-norm]. The linearization square also commutes: either route sends the entry labelled $g$ to the pullback entry labelled $gh$. These equalities on local tensors prove equality of sheaf maps, and remain true for successive base changes. Retain $G$ as indexing group even if distinct $g_T$ coincide; no factor is removed and no faithfulness is used. Open restriction is the case $T\subseteq S$.

source.place: Tags 01CD, 01CA: factorwise comparison under arbitrary pullback; no flatness assumption

proof.text: Using the tensor-sheaf construction of [def-pc-module-pullback], the pulled-back sections still generate: locally each section of $B^{\otimes n}$ is a linear combination of $s,t$, so after pullback their images generate $v^*B^{\otimes n}$, whose local generators are $1\otimes e$ for local generators $e$. The pullback compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points] and the two projections in [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] identify their pencil with the base change $Y_T\to\mathbf P^1_T$. Together with Step 7 this proves compatibility for the invariant pencil as well as for its bundle, sections and linearization. It asserts no generic-fibre faithfulness after this base change.

source.place: Tag 01NE and the following relative construction; generation checked directly from Modules Tag 01AM

proof.text: Finally, $a^m$ is the $m$-fold tensor of $a$, regarded in $L^{\otimes nm}$ by concatenation. Pullback sends it to $(g^*a)^{\otimes m}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2). In the norm construction both $\mathcal N_G(a^m)$ and $\mathcal N_G(a)^m$ are therefore the same tensor array indexed by $(g,j,r)$ with $1\leq j\leq m$, $1\leq r\leq n$: the first initially groups by $g$, the second by $j$, and the canonical power identifications group both by $(j,r)$ with the $g$ factors inside. The ordered permutation maps of [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-symmetric-monoidal] send each tensor entry to exactly that position. Equality follows on pure local tensors, hence for these sections, using the comparisons fixed by [def-sfb-pencil-orbit-bundle-norm]. If $n=0$, $a$ is a global function and the assertion is $\prod_g(g^*a)^m=(\prod_g g^*a)^m$ in the commutative ring $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. If $m=1$ it is the identity comparison.
